SMTO-FIL-0059 — SMTO's file search tool stopped with an error

GUID: bb85fb3c-a826-5069-9d38-295570737572
Slug: file-find-backend-failed
Domain: FIL · Subsystem: file

What happened

  • SMTO uses a search tool on the Gateway computer to find files by name. That tool failed or gave results SMTO couldn't trust, so no results were shown. Searching doesn't change any files.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO to search again using a plain name or simple pattern, such as "report" or "*.pdf", in one specific folder. Unusual patterns or search options can make the search tool exit with an error.
  2. Check that the folder you are searching exists and that the account SMTO uses on that computer can open it. The search tool fails when it can't read the place it was pointed at.
  3. If every search fails, ask the person who manages SMTO to run the Gateway installer again on that computer. The installer sets up the search tool the Gateway relies on.

What success looks like

  • SMTO returns a list of matching files without this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO; they include the search tool's own error text.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway's fd search process exited unsuccessfully or returned an incomplete or out-of-root path (fd_failed or invalid_backend_output).

What this means

  • The file-search process failed or returned output that does not meet its contract. The classification describes only the condition observed by the producer.

Why this can happen

  • The file search process exits unsuccessfully or produces invalid backend output.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the retained operation, condition and effect evidence before choosing a recovery action.

How to fix it

  • Read exit_code and the captured fd stderr in the result. Correct an invalid pattern or fd args; if fd itself is broken, reinstall it with the Gateway installer or python -I -m gateway_core.fd_install run with the Gateway's own Python (fd 10.3 or later) and restart the Gateway. Do not treat this as a credential failure.
  • Inspect the recorded search options, exit status and bounded backend diagnostic. Correct unsupported options or repair the selected Gateway search dependency as indicated; do not infer a credential failure.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the reported condition first; existing effect evidence and replay checks still decide whether a new attempt is permitted.

How to verify the fix

  • The reported prerequisite is satisfied and a new authorized operation returns its actual result.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a write whose external effect is still unknown.

Technical notes

  • Diagnostic presentation does not start recovery or alter authorization.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
